title: Gate map for the target of the program
reading_rule: Gates are obligations a candidate would have to meet. The list is a map of obligations and of the evidence bearing on each; it is not a claim that the gates are jointly satisfiable, and no gate is passed. The gate list follows the record of LLM Director A (GPT-6, OpenAI); evidence entries name the record or paper they come from.

gates.name: Primitive selection
gates.evidence: Finite relational structures, signed graphs and gain graphs are available as primitives; none is selected. A directed three-cycle supports both a complex-type algebra and a classical simplex (Director A, A2). Transport on a graph takes arbitrary values in arbitrary groups (G7-01-01).

gates.name: Operational event structure
gates.evidence: Unrestricted contextual tables do not select the quantum subset (TO-0). GH-1 uses walk sets as events with end vertices as records; the record role is supplied (G8).

gates.name: State and effect spaces
gates.evidence: Pure-state geometry does not fix the mixed-state theory: classical spin on S^2 (Directors A, G). GH-1 gives a Hilbert space by the Dowker-Johnston-Sorkin construction, conditional (G8-01-05).

gates.name: Transition geometry
gates.evidence: Finite homogeneous carriers excluded (G7-01-07, G7-01-09; Gelander 2013). Curvature 1 against 4 separates RP^2 from the qubit (Directors A, G; G7 Remark 5.2). Inhomogeneous nets exist with imported geometry (Directors A, B). Dense inhomogeneous subsets from gain graphs, conditional (G8-01-05). Algebraic generating data fix p only up to field automorphisms (G7-01-13).
gates.B4_additive_evidence: B4 supplies one explicit finite Z3-gain K4 construction with dense projective CP3 event-ray closure, conditional on a chosen complex character; not a physical transition-probability identification.

gates.name: Phase and complex structure
gates.evidence: Transition probabilities fix all Bargmann phases up to one conjugation, constructively (G7-01-10, G7-01-11); three overlaps alone do not (Directors A, G; Li-Wagner-Zhang 2026); the determinant of one loop does not (Director B, B2). Global conjugation of a whole model is unobservable (Director B, B2); relative orientation is fixed by composition (G7-01-15). Complex structure, symplectic form, dynamical correspondence and equality of generator and observable counts are forms of one postulate (G7-01-06, G7-01-12).

gates.name: Probability rule
gates.evidence: Squared-norm rule from invariance, second order and strong positivity on a gain graph (G8-01-02, G8-01-03). Second order is supplied. No third-order interference alone does not select quantum theory (Directors A, B, G; Barnum-Mueller-Ududec 2014).
gates.B4_additive_evidence: B4 shows squared-norm positive finite-horizon D_k need not obey cylinder-refinement compatibility. G8 generic additive impossibility requires gain-only F1 scope; closed-loop endpoint-aware additive gauge-invariants exist.

gates.name: Composition
gates.evidence: Single-system data do not fix the composite: minimal against quantum (Director B; G7-01-14); interpolated family K_t and failure of its uniform four-system extension by t(1-t)/4 (Director G); CNOT closure forces the quantum composite once a complex representation is given (Director G). Product of gain graphs gives the full tensor product with a common step count (G8-01-06).
gates.B4_additive_evidence: A3/G3 show a restricted but consistent matching-generated hierarchy and additional mixed effects are compatible with the same elementary or pure-state data; no quantum physical composition derived.

gates.name: Dynamics
gates.evidence: Static geometry does not select a generator or clock (Director A). Walk length on a gain graph is not unitary (G8 Section 9). No calibrated time.
gates.B4_additive_evidence: B4: if reciprocal-gain adjacency is scalar-unitary, it is a period-two involution; the same K4 with dense CP3 rays fails time-refinement compatibility (cross term 0->2).

gates.name: Space, causal and clock structure
gates.evidence: Ehlers-Pirani-Schild template only (Director D). No construction.

gates.name: Classical Hamiltonian mechanics
gates.evidence: Dephasing gives a stochastic channel, not a Hamiltonian flow (FAR-1; Director A). Recorded walks give the counting measure (G8-01-07). Classical and quantum pure states share a Poisson description (Landsman 1997). No derivation.

gates.name: Quantitative limit
gates.evidence: Exact homogeneity excluded; three forms of limit remain; ordering of values has to be supplied for algebraic data (G7-01-13, G8-01-08); growth condition of G8-01-05 unproved for a class of graphs.
gates.B4_additive_evidence: G8 Proposition 5.1 growth hypothesis proven for an explicit K4/Z3 graph: N_k(y,g)>=3^floor((k-10)/2) for all k>=10; this is a class-member existence proof, not a uniform physical limit law.

gates.name: Integrated claim
gates.evidence: No candidate satisfies P0 to P11. Root review G1 OPEN.

overlay_policy: No source gate states modified, no source materials overwritten; additive review only
